General Tips for Your Train Journey

  • Advance Booking: Secure better fares and preferred seats by booking early.
  • Travel Passes: Consider the Swiss Travel System ticket for discounts on international routes into Switzerland.
  • Connections: Pay attention to transfer times, especially in major hubs like Zurich and Landquart.
  • Onboard Comforts: Many trains feature dining cars, power outlets, and comfortable seating to make your journey pleasant.
  • Reliability: Swiss trains are renowned for their reliability and punctual schedules, so you can trust your connections will be on time.
  • Scenic Views: When travelling from Zurich to Davos, choose a seat on the left side facing the direction of travel for stunning views of Lake Zurich and Lake Walen (Walensee).
  • Landquart: If your journey includes a transfer in Landquart, double-check the specific section of the train you need to board, as some trains split to different destinations like St. Moritz or Scuol-Tarasp.
  • For finding the best connections and viewing train formations, the SBB website or mobile app are extremely helpful. 

Why Choose Train Travel to Davos?

Travelling by train is more than just a means to an end—it's an opportunity to make your journey part of an adventure. You'll experience some of Europe's most stunning landscapes, from rolling hills to towering alpine vistas. Plus, arriving in the heart of Davos means you're just steps away from the Drupal Mountain Camp venue.

Travel Information

Davos is accessible via multiple modes of transport. We encourage everyone to check out our sustainable travel guide to minimize your environmental impact while making your way to the event. Learn more here: Sustainable Travel Guide to Davos

Important Travel Tip: If your journey includes a transfer in Landquart, double-check the specific section of the train you need to board, as some trains split to different destinations like St. Moritz or Scuol-Tarasp.

Dan's Tip: If you're traveling from Zurich to Davos, be sure to sit on the left side facing the direction of travel for stunning views of Lake Zurich and Lake Walen (Walensee)!

Registration and Sessions

  • Registration Opens: 09:00 on March 11th, 2025
  • Sessions Start: 10:30
  • You can view the full schedule of sessions here: MountainCamp 2025 Schedule

Pre-conference Networking

The MountainCamp 2025 experience doesn’t start on March 11th—pre-conference activities will already be in full swing on the evening of March 8th! Many attendees are coming in early to network, relax, and enjoy some fun together. If you're arriving early, check out the pre-conference details here: Pre-conference Details

Social Events

MountainCamp 2025 is not just about learning and sessions. We’ve also planned some amazing social events where you can unwind and connect with fellow participants. Get a sneak peek of these events here: Social Events at MountainCamp 2025

Call for Volunteers

  • Volunteer Signup Sheet: Register Here
  • More Information: Volunteer Details
  • Join the Volunteer Discussion on Slack: Volunteer Slack Channel

Get Ready for MountainCamp 2025

MountainCamp 2025 promises to be an unforgettable event filled with learning, collaboration, and fun in one of the most beautiful parts of Switzerland. Whether you're attending to learn, network, or simply enjoy the mountain air, we're excited to see you there!

Don't forget to check the schedule, finalize your travel plans, and join the pre-conference activities. See you in Davos!

Join us for Mountain Camp 2027

From March 02–04, 2027, the open source community from Switzerland and around the world will gather in beautiful Davos for the sixth edition of Mountain Camp — celebrating 10 years since the first Drupal Mountain Camp in 2017.

This year’s theme: Humans with AI in the Loop.

Pre-conference: February 27 – March 1, 2027 — co-working, contribution sprints, skiing and networking.

  • Tuesday, March 2: Opening, fireside chat with Dries Buytaert, sessions, workshops, lightning talks and the Fondue Social
  • Wednesday, March 3: Keynote, sessions, sprints, BoFs, unconference block and a torch-lit evening walk
  • Thursday, March 4: Contribution morning, closing session and farewell lunch

Venue: Davos Congress Centre

Join us for a week of open source tech, workshops and co-working in the mountain’s fresh winter air — and enjoy everything the Swiss Alps have to offer, from snowboarding and skiing to fondue and more!

Why sponsor Mountain Camp?

Your sponsorship allows us to create a great experience — a great venue, Wi-Fi, good coffee, snacks and unforgettable social activities — for 100+ open source professionals, decision makers and contributors.

  • Community access — three days of genuine conversations with developers, agencies and digital leaders
  • Brand visibility — your logo on the website, on-site signage and social channels
  • Recruitment — meet engaged talent in an informal setting
  • Community support — Mountain Camp is a non-profit community event; sponsors make it possible

We are a community of makers, not takers — sponsoring the camp is a direct investment in open source and in a stronger community in Switzerland and beyond.

Sponsorship packages

Packages from Bronze to Platinum include benefits such as logo placement, lightning talk slots, BoF hosting, sprint mentorship, exhibition space, complimentary tickets and dedicated social posts. The full prospectus with pricing is being finalised — get in touch and we will send it to you first.

Location

Davos Congress Centre
Talstrasse 49A, 7270 Davos, Switzerland

The Davos website provides a good entry point to get yourself familiar with what the region has to offer.

How to get there

By train

The train ride from Zürich to Davos takes a little over two hours. In Landquart you change to the Rhätische Bahn, a narrow-gauge railway leading up the mountains — a very scenic ride awaits you, well worth the time! Plan your journey with SBB Online.

By car

Travelling time from Zürich Airport is about 90 minutes. Parking can be costly in Davos — please check with your hotel for a suitable arrangement.

Accommodation

We recommend staying from March 1–5, 2027 if you would like to join the main conference, and from February 27 – March 5 if you are also keen to join the pre-conference weekend.

Discounted hotel links for 2027 via Davos Tourism will be published here soon. In the meantime, use booking.com to find hotels, or the online apartment search and Airbnb for holiday apartments.

Questions about accommodation? Ask us on the Drupal Switzerland Slack.

Drupal Mountain Camp brings together people from around the world who use, develop, design, and support the Drupal, PHP and other open source platforms. Many attendees at Drupal Mountain Camp are newcomers evaluating both our platform and our community.

The Drupal Code of Conduct outlines our shared ideals and values. This document expresses how we hope to make these ideals real at our conferences and other events. Our goal is to ensure that all participants can freely and openly share ideas in a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment that encourages and inspires mutual respect and collaboration.

Come for the Software, Stay for the Community

Drupal and PHP would simply not exist without their communities. We want all attendees at Drupalcamp to have an awesome experience, both in and out of formal conference sessions.
The purpose of this document is not to restrict the diversity of ideas and expression in the Drupal community; rather, it's to raise awareness of the potential for actions that could alienate valuable members — and potential members — of the community.

We are Considerate

Drupal Mountain Camp is an international event that attracts diverse people from a wide variety of ethnic, cultural, and religious backgrounds. We acknowledge that cross-cultural communication can often be complicated and encourage everyone to consider both the impact of their actions on those with different backgrounds and experiences and the honest intentions of those who may have unknowingly caused offense.

We are Welcoming

One of the greatest strengths of the Drupal and PHP communities is our inclusiveness. Making all attendees feel welcome and included at Drupalcamp is everyone’s job, including exhibitors and sponsors.

We are Respectful

Sponsors, volunteers, speakers, attendees, and other participants should strive to treat all people with dignity and respect, regardless of their culture, religion, physical appearance, disability, race, ethnicity, gender, or sexual orientation.

We are Collaborative

If and when misunderstandings occur, we encourage people to work things out between themselves whenever that is safe for them to do (see the next points for dealing with harassment). People are encouraged to take responsibility for their words and actions and listen to constructively-presented criticism with an open mind, courtesy, and respect.

When We Disagree, We Consult Others

If people are unable to work out issues between themselves, they are encouraged to seek the advice of a mutually trusted third party or a designated community volunteer to help mediate.

When We Need it, We Ask for Help

We do not tolerate harassment of conference participants in any form. If you feel threatened or violated as a result of intimidating, harassing, abusive, discriminatory, derogatory or demeaning conduct, please immediately notify a conference staff member. Likewise, please immediately notify a staff member if you notice that someone else is being subjected to such behavior.

Contact the Organizers

When contacting the Organizers about an incident, we need all available information: who's involved, what specifically caused the incident, what steps were taken to resolve it prior to contacting the Organizers, any log files or other data to corroborate the event, etc.

If the matter is urgent, please contact one of the following individuals on-site:

Dan Lemon (dan+drupal@danlemon.com, Twitter: @dan2k3k4)

Josef Kruckenberg (dasjogibtsnet@gmail.com, Website: dasjo)

Sinduri Guntupalli (sinduri.g@gmail.com, LinkedIN: sinduri-guntupalli-307542131)

The Drupal Mountain Camp team wants everyone to feel safe for the duration of the conference. If necessary, conference volunteers are empowered to take appropriate actions that may include, but are not limited to, warnings, expulsion from the conference without refund, and referrals to venue security or local law enforcement.

We’re All in this Together

Thanks for making Drupal Mountain Camp awesome for everyone!

The Drupal Mountain Camp Code of Conduct is a derivative of the DrupalCon Los Angeles Code of Conduct and is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License. It is available for others to use and adapt for their own events.
